name: Vantablack Ops Liaison Jacket
description:
Vantablack doesn't issue tactical uniforms in the traditional sense. The Ops Liaison Jacket is designed to look like civilian outerwear — a trim, mid-length coat in flat matte black that reads as expensive street fashion until it doesn't. The exterior fabric is woven with Vantablack's signature light-absorption compound, not to the extreme of true VantaMat applications, but enough to make the wearer visually recede in low-light environments, reducing silhouette definition and making optical tracking systems struggle for clean acquisition. The jacket carries no visible corporate branding; the only identifying marker is a microscopic spectral tag in the left cuff, readable only by Vantablack-issued scanners.

Internally, the jacket is a different garment entirely. A network of sensor-filament threads maps the wearer's immediate environment and feeds data through a BCI port concealed within the collar seam. Pockets are shielded against RF scanning, and the lining includes a signal-dampening mesh that limits the wearer's electronic signature in monitored spaces. The jacket is cut to read as civilian across Tier 3 through 5 environments — it is not designed for the Shelf, where anyone wearing something that expensive without obvious corp affiliation becomes a target. Vantablack personnel who operate in lower tiers are typically issued cover garments to wear over the jacket. Possession without authorization is deeply inadvisable.
cultural_context: Vantablack has a reputation for existing in spaces it officially doesn't occupy. The Ops Liaison Jacket is part of that reputation — a garment that signals intelligence presence without confirming it. In GLMZ's corporate circles, being approached by someone in a coat that eats light is understood as a meeting you don't discuss afterward.
story_hooks: A counterfeit version of the Ops Liaison Jacket is circulating in Tier 3 markets — it has the visual profile but none of the electronics, and someone wearing one is about to walk into a situation where Vantablack will assume they're an operative.
The spectral tag in a recovered jacket's cuff doesn't match any active Vantablack operative ID — it belongs to someone who was officially declared dead two years ago.

A journalist investigating corporate surveillance purchases what they believe is a replica jacket for a story on Vantablack's visual-stealth tech, and discovers the 'replica' is feeding data to an unknown receiver.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively simple mid-length coat that seems to absorb light itself. Silhouette is lean and tailored, sitting just below the hip with a subtle A-line that allows mobility without bulk. On first glance it reads as high-end civilian streetwear—expensive, understated, forgettable. In low light, the wearer's edges blur and soften, making the eye slip past them. The coat seems to exist in slight visual deficit to its surroundings.
physical_description.fit: Trim but not restrictive. Shoulders sit precisely at the natural shoulder point with minimal padding. Sleeves are tapered to the wrist, allowing for augmented limbs or standard anatomy without binding. The body is cut straight through the torso with minimal waist definition—functional rather than fashionable, though fashion is the disguise.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade synthetic weave impregnated with Vantablack's proprietary light-absorption compound. The exterior is matte to the point of appearing slightly textured at close range, though direct light reflection is virtually nonexistent. The lining is a dense RF-dampening mesh woven into treated synthetic silk.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and almost frictionless to the touch on the exterior, with a subtle grain barely perceptible when run against the light. The compound creates a faint static charge that repels dust. The interior lining has a fine waffle-weave pattern that dissipates body heat and provides grip points for the sensor-filament network beneath.
physical_description.color_scheme: Absolute matte black—the kind of black that seems to have depth rather than surface. No accent colors, no branding, no visible stitching on the exterior (seams are heat-fused). The only visible break is the subtle iridescence of the concealed spectral tag location in the left cuff under specific scanner wavelengths (invisible to human sight).
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snaps concealed beneath a false front placket, allowing rapid opening without audible clicks. The snaps are encrypted to Vantablack's biometric key. A single concealed zipper runs the full length of the front seam beneath the magnetic locks, allowing for rapid access to interior pockets.
distinctive_features: Microscopic spectral tag embedded in left cuff—readable only by Vantablack-issued scanners
Hidden BCI port concealed in collar seam, flush with the neck lining
Internal sensor-filament network mapping immediate environment
RF-shielded pockets with magnetic closures—no external seams visible
Signal-dampening mesh lining that reduces electronic signature in monitored spaces
Completely seamless construction on the exterior; all seams are interior-facing or heat-fused
Subtle ergonomic shaping allowing for unrestricted arm movement and augmentation accommodation
The fabric appears to 'drink' light, creating a visual receding effect
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 material quality and construction, but designed to masquerade as Tier 3-4 civilian wear. The real cost is in materials and embedded systems, not visible prestige markers. Possession outside official channels is treated as Tier 5 criminal acquisition.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is an intelligence operative's outer layer—the uniform of people who aren't supposed to exist in a space but do. Wearing it signals either direct employment by Vantablack or very serious problems. In GLMZ's corporate circles, seeing someone in a coat that eats light is understood as a conversation you won't remember afterward, and possibly one you shouldn't have had. Among street-level workers (Tier 4-5), the coat marks the wearer as either corpo operatives or salvagers who've acquired something far too advanced for their layer.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine. The material resists wear, and any damage compromises the light-absorption properties and sensor network. Worn examples are immediately pulled from service and replaced. If you see a creased or weathered version, it's a coverall someone has thrown over the real thing.
